title: Helicopters Airdrop Food as Cyclone Arnab Flooding Maroons Thousands in Odisha
excerpt: Four helicopters are dropping food packets at 21 locations in flood-hit Ganjam, where about 43,000 people have been affected, more than 23,000 evacuated and no casualties have been reported so far after Cyclone Arnab dumped 118 percent excess rainfall in three days.
body:
• Four armed-forces helicopters have begun airdropping food packets at 21 locations in Odisha's Ganjam district, where floodwaters from Cyclone Arnab have cut off villages for more than 24 hours.
  • About 43,000 people have been affected across 22 blocks of Ganjam; 23,323 have been evacuated to 352 relief centres, and the government says no casualties have been reported so far.
  • Ganjam received 118 percent above-normal rainfall in three days; more than 100 of the 313 rescue teams deployed across Odisha are working in Ganjam and Gajapati.
  • A central team will visit Odisha on November 2 to assess flood damage, and an additional Rs 20 crore has been released to Ganjam for relief work.

Four helicopters of the armed forces have started airdropping food packets at 21 locations in Odisha's flood-hit Ganjam district, as rescue teams struggle to reach villages marooned by waters from the overflowing Rushikulya river after Cyclone Arnab brought incessant rain to south Odisha, according to Sambad English.

The airdrops cover areas including Hinjili, Chikiti, Purushottampur, Sheragada, Dharakote, Aska and Belaguntha, where road connectivity has been disrupted and even boats cannot operate against the current. Personnel stationed at the drop points collect the packets and distribute them to stranded residents.

"It was not possible to reach the affected people even by using modern boats due to the heavy current of flowing water."

— Suresh Pujari, Odisha Revenue and Disaster Management Minister

The Scale of the Flooding

Revenue and Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari said about 50,000 people had been severely affected in Ganjam in the initial assessment, while district figures put the affected population at around 43,000 across 22 blocks, with 23,323 people evacuated to 352 relief centres, The Hindu BusinessLine reported. Gajapati and Kandhamal districts have also suffered damage.

https://x.com/the_hindu/status/2116136641421099070

Ganjam recorded 118 percent excess rainfall over the three-day period. Odisha as a whole received 132 mm of rainfall between October 1 and October 30, 18.7 percent above normal. Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi, who also holds the Water Resources portfolio, expressed concern over the unexpectedly heavy rainfall in Ganjam and Gajapati and left on Friday afternoon for an aerial survey of the two districts.

Rescue Operations on the Ground

Of the 313 rescue teams deployed across the state, more than 100 are engaged in Ganjam and Gajapati, including Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF) and National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) personnel and fire services teams. Fire services personnel rescued 303 people in Berhampur, 359 in Chhatrapur, 31 in Gajapati and 91 in Kandhamal, according to district reports.

On Thursday, an Indian Coast Guard ALH Mk-III helicopter winched six people to safety — including two women, two children and an elderly person — from a flooded public health centre at Jagmohan in Ganjam. The state had requested Coast Guard assistance on October 29 to airlift stranded people and drop food in pockets boats could not reach. With rainfall subsiding over the past 12 hours, rescue teams expect to distribute cooked food by boat in areas where people remain surrounded by water, and airdrop packets are carrying up to 4,500 kg of grain.

What Happens Next

The flood situation in Ganjam is gradually improving as water drains from inundated areas such as Chhatrapur, district officials said, and schools in the affected areas remain shut. A central team will visit Odisha on November 2 to assess the damage, Sambad English reported — the assessment that normally precedes central relief assistance. The Special Relief Commissioner's office has released an additional Rs 20 crore to Ganjam for relief and rescue work.

For families with relatives in the affected blocks, the district relief centres are the first point of contact: 352 centres are operating in Ganjam, and relief materials have been distributed since Thursday, Collector V. Keerthi Vasan said.
